questions.q: Who was the last Tsar of Russia?
questions.explanation: Nicholas II ruled until his abdication in 1917 and was executed in 1918.

questions.q: Which country has the most natural lakes in the world?
questions.explanation: Canada contains more natural lakes than any other country, including most of the world's freshwater lakes.

questions.q: What is the derivative of x^2 with respect to x?
questions.explanation: Using the power rule, the derivative of x^2 is 2x.

questions.q: Who wrote 'In Search of Lost Time'?
questions.explanation: Marcel Proust wrote this seven-volume novel, published between 1913 and 1927.

questions.q: What is the approximate speed of light in a vacuum, in km/s?
questions.explanation: Light travels at approximately 299,792 kilometers per second in a vacuum.

questions.q: Which treaty formally ended World War I?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Versailles, signed in 1919, formally ended World War I.

questions.q: Which African country is commonly cited as never having been formally colonized?
questions.explanation: Ethiopia successfully resisted colonization, aside from a brief Italian occupation from 1936 to 1941.

questions.q: What is the value of Euler's number (e), rounded to 2 decimal places?
questions.explanation: Euler's number e is approximately 2.71828, which rounds to 2.72.
Fyodor Dostoevsky published 'Crime and Punishment' in 1866.

questions.q: Which particle mediates the electromagnetic force?
questions.explanation: The photon is the force-carrying particle of electromagnetism.

questions.q: Which philosopher was the personal tutor of Alexander the Great?
questions.explanation: Aristotle tutored Alexander the Great starting around 343 BC.

questions.q: What is the deepest known point in Earth's oceans?
questions.explanation: The Mariana Trench's Challenger Deep is the deepest known point in the ocean, about 11,000 meters deep.

questions.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a pentagon?
questions.explanation: A pentagon's interior angles sum to (5-2) x 180° = 540°.
Dante Alighieri wrote 'The Divine Comedy' in the early 14th century.
